item.title: Terrington St Clement man cleared of assault charges
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Terrington St Clement man cleared of assault charges
A 22-year-old man from Terrington St Clement has been cleared of assault and stalking charges at Lynn Magistrates’ Court. Ryley Dale, of Waterloo Road, had faced allegations including intentional strangulation, criminal damage, and harassment of an ex-partner between 2023 and 2024. During a summary trial on Wednesday, November 11, the Crown Prosecution Service offered no evidence, leading to the charges being dropped.
Mr. Dale previously gained public attention in September 2024 for his actions during a house fire in Gaywood. He was credited with helping to save four people from the property on Lynn Road after forcing entry to the building.

item.title: Closure orders granted for shops in March and Whittlesey
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Closure orders granted for shops in March and Whittlesey
Two shops in Fenland have been closed following a multi-agency operation targeting the sale of illegal goods. Cambridge Magistrates’ Court granted the orders on Friday after police and partner agencies visited 60 businesses across the region in October.
The March Shop on High Street is now fully closed until December 12. Meanwhile, the Whittlesey Local Store on Market Street faces a partial closure until February 13, with a ban on the sale or storage of tobacco and nicotine products. The operation, known as ‘Operation Machinize’, resulted in the seizure of thousands of illicit items, including cigarettes and vapes. Authorities say investigations into various offences at several other premises remain ongoing.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
New museum approved for King’s Lynn’s Chequer House
Plans have been approved to open a new museum inside the historic Chequer House on King Street in King’s Lynn. West Norfolk Council granted permission for a change of use application submitted by Miniscatter Ltd. The project involves converting existing second-floor offices at the rear of the building into a museum space.
The approved plans include the removal of modern partitions to create a contemporary gallery area for displays. Planning officers noted that the development will provide a new cultural facility for the town while maintaining employment use at the site. Officials confirmed the changes will not negatively impact the character of the listed building or the surrounding conservation area.

item.title: Winter appeal launched to support West Norfolk charities
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Winter appeal launched to support West Norfolk charities
A new winter appeal has been launched to support homeless and vulnerable people across West Norfolk. Now in its eighth year, the campaign is raising funds for the Lynn Night Shelter, The Purfleet Trust, and food banks in King’s Lynn and Downham Market.
Organisers are requesting financial donations rather than food items to help these charities cover essential costs, including utilities and staff. The appeal runs until the end of January. Donations can be dropped off at the Your Local Paper office at 17 Tuesday Market Place in King’s Lynn, or delivered directly to the charities involved. Each organisation is seeking community support to maintain their services during the colder months.

King’s Lynn Academy addresses reports of rodent activity
King’s Lynn Academy has confirmed it identified isolated rodent activity on its premises. Following reports of sightings in the school’s kitchen, cafeteria, and a food technology classroom, the academy says immediate action was taken. Specialist contractors were appointed to implement control measures and enhanced monitoring.
The school is working closely with an Environmental Health officer, who has confirmed that the steps taken are appropriate and the situation is being managed effectively. The academy maintains that the health and safety of students and staff remains a priority, and the school continues to operate as normal.

The film follows the traditional narrative of the miserly Scrooge being visited by three spirits on Christmas Eve. While the story remains largely faithful to the original masterpiece, this version provides additional background on the development of the protagonist's character. Tickets are available now for those looking to catch the festive feature at the local cinema.

item.description:

Seven million pound investment at King’s Lynn port
A seven million pound investment has seen a new industrial facility open at the Port of King’s Lynn. Associated British Ports has transformed a previously unused site at the junction of Edward Benefer Way and Estuary Road into a storage and processing hub for the company Azelis.
The purpose-built site includes over 4,000 square metres of storage space and a heavy-duty concrete yard. The project, constructed by Britcon, aims to improve cargo handling and supply chain efficiency in the region. North West Norfolk MP James Wild has welcomed the development, describing the project as a significant vote of confidence in the local economy and the port's role in supporting West Norfolk trade.

item.title: New online tool ranks Norfolk postcodes by safety
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
New online tool ranks Norfolk postcodes by safety
A new interactive tool has been launched to rank UK postcodes based on their safety in the event of a national attack. The "Doomsday" checker assigns properties a score out of 100 and a safety rating from A to G, based on proximity to military bases, power stations, and other infrastructure.
In Norfolk, North Norfolk was identified as the safest region, with Cromer receiving a top rating of 10A. Conversely, areas near RAF Marham and Norwich were flagged as higher risk due to their proximity to military and utility sites. The tool, which considers factors like weather and access to medical care, is available for public use at inspectorwalls.com/doomsday.

item.title: King’s Lynn prepares for Christmas lights switch-on this Sunday
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn prepares for Christmas lights switch-on this Sunday
King’s Lynn will host its annual Christmas lights switch-on this Sunday, November 22, in the Tuesday Market Place. The event begins at 2pm with an afternoon of live music and entertainment, featuring performances from local school choirs and singer Sarah Mai. Hosted by Jeremy Durrant, the celebrations will culminate with the official switch-on at 5pm, performed by the Mayor of West Norfolk, Councillor Steve Bearshaw.
Further festive activities are scheduled for the town throughout December, including a Christmas market and Santa-themed events. Meanwhile, residents in Downham and Hunstanton can look forward to their own local switch-on celebrations, which are set to take place the following weekend on Sunday, November 29.
